desc.es: Describir personalidad con matices: adjetivos compuestos, intensificadores y lenguaje tentativo

grammarIntro.es:
Hablar de la impresión que da alguien

come across as + adj./sust.He comes across as rather smug. (da la impresión de ser)
strike sb asShe struck me as very perceptive. (me pareció)
give the impression of + -ingHe gives the impression of being shy, but he isn't.

Adjetivos compuestos

Muy productivos en inglés: self- (self-conscious, self-centred), -minded (open-minded, narrow-minded), -tempered (bad-tempered), -going (easy-going), -hearted (kind-hearted).

Colocaciones adverbio + adjetivo

deeply religious / offended · utterly ruthless · painfully shy · mildly amused · fiercely independent · blissfully unaware
En C1 se valora el matiz: en lugar de very shy, usa painfully shy; en lugar de very independent, fiercely independent.
Falsos amigos: sensible = sensato (sensible en español = sensitive); sympathetic = comprensivo (simpático = nice, friendly); eventual = final.

desc.es: La inversión tras expresiones negativas y restrictivas para dar énfasis

grammarIntro.es:
¿Qué es la inversión?

Cuando una frase empieza por un adverbio negativo o restrictivo, el orden pasa a ser el de una pregunta: auxiliar + sujeto + verbo. Es propia del registro formal y escrito, y da mucho énfasis.

Never (before) / Rarely / SeldomNever have I seen such chaos.
Not only … but (also)Not only did he lie, but he also blamed me.
No sooner … thanNo sooner had I sat down than the phone rang.
Hardly / Scarcely / Barely … whenHardly had we arrived when it started to rain.
Only then / Only after / Only whenOnly then did I realise my mistake.
Not untilNot until the next day did she call.
LittleLittle did she know what was waiting for her.
Under no circumstances / On no accountUnder no circumstances should you open this door.
Si no hay auxiliar (presente o pasado simple), se usa do / does / did: Rarely does she complain.
Con Only after / Not until la inversión va en la oración principal, no en la subordinada: ✓ Only after he left did I notice. ✗ Only after did he leave I noticed.

gnames: Only then / Only after / Not until

desc.es: Oraciones escindidas (cleft sentences) para destacar información

grammarIntro.es:
Partir la frase para dar énfasis

Una cleft sentence divide una oración en dos partes para poner el foco en un elemento.

It is/was X that/who …Tom broke the vase → It was Tom who broke the vase (no yo).
What + sujeto + verbo + is/was …I need a holiday → What I need is a holiday.
All (that) … is/was …All I want is some peace and quiet. (lo único que)
The thing / reason / place / person …The reason (why) I left was the noise.
What happened was (that) …What happened was that the train broke down.
What + sujeto + did was … (acciones)What she did was (to) call the police.
Para destacar una acción usa What … do/did is/was + infinitivo: What you should do is apologise.
«Lo que» al principio de frase es What, no That ni Which: ✗ That I don't understand is… → ✓ What I don't understand is…

title.es: No hacía falta que te molestaras

desc.es: Modales avanzados: deducción, obligación en el pasado, crítica y usos especiales

grammarIntro.es:
Necesidad en el pasado: dos significados distintos

needn't have + participioYou needn't have bought wine. (lo compraste, pero no hacía falta)
didn't need to + infinitivoI didn't need to buy wine. (no hacía falta, y normalmente no lo compré)

Probabilidad con matices

be bound to / be sure toIt's bound to rain. (seguro que)
may/might/could wellShe may well be right. (es muy posible)
might as well / may as wellThe bus has gone; we might as well walk. (ya puestos)
can't have / must haveHe can't have forgotten; I reminded him twice.

Planes que no se cumplieron

We were to have married in June, but the wedding was cancelled. (íbamos a…)
should tras It's strange / odd / surprising that expresa sorpresa: It's odd that he should say that.
«Debe de haber» = must have (deducción), no should have (crítica): She must have left (seguro que se fue) / She should have left (debería haberse ido).

title.es: Encargar que te hagan las cosas

grammarIntro.es:
Estructuras causativas

have / get + objeto + participioI had my car repaired. (me lo arreglaron)
have + persona + infinitivo sin toI'll have the plumber look at it.
get + persona + to + infinitivoI got my brother to help me. (conseguí que)
have sth done (algo malo que te pasa)She had her bag stolen. (le robaron el bolso)

Pasiva con verbos de opinión

Muy usada en noticias: It is said / believed / thought / reported that… o Sujeto + is said to + infinitivo.

The minister is believed to be abroad. (presente)
The thieves are thought to have escaped by car. (pasado → to have + participio)

Infinitivo y gerundio pasivos

I hate being interrupted. · She expects to be paid on time. · The house needs painting (= needs to be painted).
«Me corté el pelo» en la peluquería es I had my hair cut; I cut my hair significa que lo hiciste tú.

desc.es: Condicionales avanzadas: inversión, alternativas a if y condicionales implícitas

grammarIntro.es:
Condicionales con inversión (formal)

Se elimina if y se invierte el auxiliar:

Had I known, I would have come.= If I had known…
Should you need help, call me.= If you (should) need… (formal, por si acaso)
Were I in your position, I'd resign.= If I were…
Were he to find out, he'd be furious.= If he found out…

Alternativas a if

Provided / Providing (that) you pay on time, there's no problem.
As long as / So long as you're happy, I'm happy.
On condition that he apologises.
Supposing you lost your job, what would you do?
But for your help, we'd have failed. (de no ser por)
Hurry up, otherwise we'll miss the train.
If it weren't for (presente) / If it hadn't been for (pasado) = de no ser por. Con inversión: Had it not been for the rain…
En la inversión negativa not va detrás del sujeto y sin contracción: ✓ Had I not seen it… ✗ Hadn't I seen it…

desc.es: Verbos frasales de nivel avanzado en contextos de trabajo y relaciones

grammarIntro.es:
Separables e inseparables

Con los separables, si el objeto es un pronombre va en medio: turn it down (✗ turn down it). Los inseparables nunca se parten: look into it, run into her.

bring upsacar (un tema); criar
rule outdescartar
iron outlimar (problemas)
play downquitar importancia
phase outeliminar gradualmente
step downdimitir, apartarse
live up toestar a la altura de
brush up onrepasar, refrescar

Sustantivos a partir de phrasal verbs

break down → a breakdown · set back → a setback · turn out → the turnout · come out → the outcome · cut back → cutbacks · take over → a takeover
Los de tres partes (put up with, come up with, get on with, look forward to) son siempre inseparables y el objeto va al final.
✗ I'll think it over it. ✓ I'll think it over. Con el pronombre en medio, no se repite al final.

title.es: La puesta en marcha del plan

desc.es: Nominalización y registro formal: pasar de un estilo verbal a uno nominal

grammarIntro.es:
De verbos a sustantivos

El inglés académico y administrativo prefiere los sustantivos a los verbos: concentra más información y suena más objetivo.

The council decided to close the library, and residents protested.
→ The council's decision to close the library provoked protests from residents.
implement → implementationassess → assessment
comply → compliancefail → failure
reluctant → reluctanceable → ability

Verbos de apoyo

make a decision / a contribution · carry out research / an investigation · give consideration to · reach an agreement · raise a concern

Registro formal

getobtain
startcommence
tryendeavour
beforeprior to
aftersubsequent to
helpfacilitate / assist
No abuses: demasiadas nominalizaciones vuelven el texto pesado. En una carta formal busca equilibrio, no acumules -tion tras -tion.

desc.es: Lenguaje tentativo (hedging), distanciamiento y lenguaje vago

grammarIntro.es:
¿Por qué suavizar?

En inglés académico y profesional, las afirmaciones rotundas suenan arrogantes o poco rigurosas. El hedging permite expresar prudencia.

seem / appear toThe results appear to confirm the theory.
It would seem / appear thatIt would seem that there has been a mistake.
It could be argued thatIt could be argued that the plan is too expensive.
tend toYoung people tend to be more flexible.
to some extent / to a certain degreeI agree to some extent.
arguablyShe is arguably the best writer of her generation. (se podría decir que)

Lenguaje vago (informal)

There were twenty or so people. · It's sort of blueish. · Come at six-ish. · We talked about work, family and so on / and stuff like that.
Combinar mecanismos refuerza la cautela: This maypartly explain why…
apparently = al parecer, según dicen; no significa «aparentemente» en el sentido de «a simple vista falso». Para eso usa seemingly u on the surface.

desc.es: Elipsis y sustitución para evitar repeticiones

grammarIntro.es:
Sustituir con so / not

I think so / I don't think socreo que sí / creo que no

"Are you coming?" "I'd love to." (no se repite come)

desc.es: Conectores avanzados de contraste, concesión, causa y consecuencia

grammarIntro.es:
Contraste y concesión

albeit (+ adj./adv.)a small, albeit important, change (aunque)
whereas / whilstI love cities, whereas my wife prefers the country.
nonetheless / nevertheless / even soIt was risky. Nevertheless, we did it.
Much as + sujeto + verboMuch as I like him, I can't trust him. (por mucho que)
Adj. + as/though + sujeto + verboTired as she was, she kept going. (aunque estaba cansada)
admittedly / grantedAdmittedly, it's expensive, but it's worth it.

Causa y consecuencia

Owing to / Due to / In view of the weather, the match was cancelled.
Given that nobody came, we left early.
Costs rose; hence the price increase. (de ahí)
The data was incomplete, and thus unreliable.
irrespective of / regardless of = independientemente de: Everyone pays the same, irrespective of income.
Owing to va seguido de sustantivo o -ing, no de una oración: ✗ owing to it rained → ✓ owing to the rain / owing to the fact that it rained.

desc.es: Formación de palabras avanzada: prefijos, sufijos y cambios de categoría

grammarIntro.es:
Prefijos con significado

mis- (mal)misunderstand, misinterpret, misplace, mislead
under- / over- (poco / demasiado)underestimate, overcook, overrated, underpaid
out- (superar)outnumber, outlive, outgrow, outperform
counter- (contra)counterproductive, counterattack, counterpart
re- (otra vez)rethink, rediscover, recharge, reassure

Sufijos que cambian la categoría

Verbo: wide → widen, strong → strengthen, modern → modernise
Sustantivo abstracto: child → childhood, friend → friendship, close → closeness, simple → simplicity, likely → likelihood
Adjetivo: create → creative, danger → dangerous, recognise → recognisable, flex → flexible
En los ejercicios de word formation de la EOI, fíjate en qué categoría pide el hueco (artículo delante → sustantivo; verbo be delante → adjetivo) y si la frase necesita sentido negativo o plural.
Ojo con la ortografía: strong → strength → strengthen, long → length → lengthen, high → height → heighten.

desc.es: Recursos de énfasis y actitud: do enfático, adverbios de comentario, so/such, whatever/however

grammarIntro.es:
Do enfático

En afirmativa, do / does / did + infinitivo refuerza o contradice: I do like your dress! (¡me encanta de verdad!) · She did call; you just didn't hear it.

Adverbios de comentario

Muestran tu actitud ante toda la frase y suelen ir al principio con coma:

Frankly, I don't care. · Understandably, she was upset. · Ironically, the fire station burnt down. · Regrettably, we cannot accept your offer.

so / such

It was so cold (that) we stayed in. · It was such a cold day (that)… · such beautiful weather (incontable, sin a)

whatever / however / whoever

Whatever you do, don't tell her. (hagas lo que hagas)
However hard I try, I can't remember. (por mucho que)
Whoever wins, it'll be a great match.
Not that… introduce una aclaración: He didn't invite me — not that I wanted to go. (no es que quisiera ir)
✗ such cold weather day; ✓ such a cold day / such cold weather. Such necesita sustantivo; so, adjetivo o adverbio solos.

desc.es: Pasado irreal y deseos: would rather, it's time, as if, if only, wish

grammarIntro.es:
Pasado con valor de presente

would rather + sujeto + pasadoI'd rather you didn't smoke here. (preferiría que no)
it's (high / about) time + sujeto + pasadoIt's high time you got a job. (ya va siendo hora)
as if / as though + pasadoHe talks as if he knew everything.
suppose / imagine + pasadoSuppose you lost your job…

wish / if only

+ pasado (presente irreal)I wish I had more time.
+ pasado perfecto (lamento pasado)If only I had listened to you!
+ would (queja sobre otros)I wish you would stop interrupting.
Con el mismo sujeto, would rather va con infinitivo sin to: I'd rather stay at home. Con sujeto distinto, pasado: I'd rather you stayed.
No se dice I wish I would… para uno mismo: ✗ I wish I would be taller → ✓ I wish I were taller.
